post.summary: Copy a chat: up to a message, or as a new version of an edited prompt
post.description: With `throughMessageId`, a separate chat holding the history through that message. With `editSeq`, a new version of the same conversation (ADR-0038): the history before the prompt at that seq, which the next generate replaces.

post.summary: Stream an assistant reply over SSE
post.description: Returns text/event-stream. Frames: start, research, delta, sources, tool_use, tool_result, done, error. Each frame carries an SSE `id`. Disconnecting does not cancel the run: reattach with GET /chats/:id/stream, cancel with POST /stop.

get.summary: Reattach to this chat's running (or just finished) reply over SSE
get.description: Replays the run's frames after `after` (the SSE `id` of the last frame received; omit for all), then streams live frames until the run ends. 404 `no_active_run` when this instance holds no run for the chat: read the chat for the persisted reply.

post.summary: Cancel the run in progress on this chat
Rate an assistant reply

get.summary: A reply's turn log, as a text file (ADR-0050)
get.description: What the reply sent and did: the model, the attachments as they went (PDF page images included), the tools and skills offered, and every tool call with its input and result.

patch.summary: Rename a project, edit its instructions, or pin it

delete.description: Chats in the project are kept and detached from it, because a conversation has value independent of the folder it was filed under.

post.summary: Set the manual order of projects
post.description: Send the ids in the order you want them. Any project omitted keeps its current position and may therefore end up interleaved; send the full list to be sure.

post.summary: Upload a file into a project and index it
post.description: multipart/form-data with a single `file` part. Answers 202 with the file queued; poll `GET /projects/:id/files/:fileId` until it is `ready`, `unsupported` or `failed`.

get.summary: Files in a project
One project file, for polling while it is read
get.description: While the file is being read this wakes the worker and holds up to FILE_POLL_HOLD_MS for its status to move.

put.summary: Replace a project file with a new version
put.description: multipart/form-data with a single `file` part (Stage 9 G42, D1 #38). The file keeps its id; its old bytes, chunks and derivative are replaced once the new version is read. Answers 202, as upload.

delete.summary: Remove a file and its chunks

get.summary: Download the stored bytes of a project file

post.summary: Re-extract and re-chunk a file
post.description: Useful after a failed extraction. Queues the file to be read again (202, poll the file); existing chunks are replaced, not added to.

get.summary: Rank this project’s indexed chunks against a query
get.description: Lexical (BM25) ranking over extracted text. This is not semantic search: a query that shares no words with a document will not match it.

get.summary: Sources saved to a project

post.summary: Save a source to a project

post.summary: Create an artifact with its first version

get.summary: An artifact with the content of its current version

patch.summary: Rename an artifact or move it between a project and a chat
patch.description: Content is never changed here. Use POST /artifacts/:id/versions for that.

delete.summary: Delete an artifact and all of its versions
delete.description: Hard delete. Messages that referenced it keep their `artifactId`, which resolves to a 404 rather than rewriting conversation history.

post.summary: Append a new version and point the artifact at it

get.summary: Version history, newest first (metadata only)

post.summary: Restore an earlier version by appending a copy of it
post.description: History is never truncated: restoring version 2 of five creates version 6 with version 2’s content, so the restore can itself be undone.

post.summary: Export a markdown version as a real .xlsx/.docx/.pptx file
post.description: Deterministic: parses the tables, headings, and bullet lists already in the source version's Markdown — it does not ask a model to produce anything new. See ADR-0004, item 8. Filed into history as a new binary version, downloadable at GET /artifacts/:id/versions/:version/download — it never becomes the artifact’s current (editable) version, which stays on the markdown draft it was derived from.

get.summary: A spreadsheet version as sheets of typed cells, for the preview panel
Download the bytes of a binary (exported) version
Token and cost totals for today, this month, and all time
Current limits and how much of them is spent

patch.summary: Set output ceiling, token budgets, warning threshold, and timezone
patch.description: Send null for a budget to clear it. Budgets are enforced by reservation before a call, so lowering one below what is already spent blocks the next request rather than cancelling one in flight.

get.summary: Usage for each assistant message in a chat
get.description: The chat transcript omits usage to stay lean. Fetch it here when the per-message token row is actually being shown.

get.summary: Download the raw usage records as CSV
get.description: One row per generation attempt, including cancellations and failures. Empty cost cells mean no price is configured for that model, not zero cost.

get.summary: Every stored preference for the signed-in user

patch.description: Only the fields you send change. Token budgets and the output ceiling are not accepted here — use PATCH /usage/limits.

post.summary: Upload a file to attach to a message
post.description: multipart/form-data with a single `file` part. Returns an id to pass in `attachmentIds` on the next generate call. Unattached uploads are not kept forever.

post.summary: Start an upload of a file to attach to a message
post.description: For files of any size up to ATTACHMENT_MAX_BYTES. Returns the attachment (status `uploading`) and where to PUT its bytes; with GCS storage that is the bucket itself, so the file never passes through this API. Then call `POST /files/:id/complete`.

put.summary: Receive the bytes of an upload (local storage only)
put.description: Only handed out by `POST /files/uploads` when storage cannot take the upload directly. The body is the raw file, exactly as many bytes as were declared.

post.summary: Finish an upload: check the bytes arrived, then read the file
post.description: Checks every byte arrived, then queues the file to be read and answers 202 with status `queued`; poll `GET /files/:id` until it is `ready` or `failed` (with an `errorCode`). With FILE_PIPELINE=sync the file is read in this request and the answer (200) is final.

post.summary: Read a failed file again
post.description: For a `failed` file (Stage 9 RETRY): queues it to be read again (202, poll `GET /files/:id`), or reads it in the request with FILE_PIPELINE=sync (200).

post.summary: Attach an existing project file to a message
post.description: Reuses the project file's stored bytes rather than re-uploading. Returns an id to pass in `attachmentIds` on the next generate call, same as `POST /files`.

get.summary: Attachment metadata

delete.description: Refused once the file is attached to a message: removing it would leave a transcript claiming context the model can no longer be shown.

get.summary: Download the stored bytes of an attachment
A spreadsheet attachment as sheets of typed cells, for the preview panel
get.description: Every sheet's first 200 rows and 50 columns. Only .xlsx.

post.summary: Discard your own uploads that were never attached to a message
post.description: Scoped to the signed-in user. Safe to call on sign-out or app start; it only touches rows with no message and a creation time older than the cutoff.
